# Sūcijātaka (Ja 387)
**ID:** Ja 387
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Sūcijātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja387
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sūcijātaka* (Ja 387), translated as *Needles*, is a birth-story related by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana concerning the perfection of wisdom [SuttaCentral]. The narrative recounts how the Bodhisatta, born as a clever young smith (*kammāraputta*), was skilled in devices and sought the hand of the daughter of a wealthy guild-leader of smiths (*kammārajeṭṭhaka*) [SuttaCentral; Dutt 1956; Loukota]. Demonstrating exquisite craftsmanship in fashioning needles, he earns her hand in marriage and eventually succeeds to the position of guild-head of the smith village (*kammāragāma*) [Fausböll 1883; Loukota]. In the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the smith's daughter as Rāhulamātā and the skilled young smith as himself [Fausböll 1883]. Scholars have cited the text for its illumination of ancient craft guilds, specialized artisan villages, and corporate headmen (*jeṭṭhaka*) [Dutt 1956; Loukota].
SuttaCentral notes thematic resembling parallels in the *Mahāvastu* (*The Jātaka of Amarā, the Smith’s Daughter*, Mvu 44) as well as the *Vidhurajātaka* (Ja 546) [SuttaCentral]. Maurice Winternitz notes that the motif of an artistic smith making needles so fine that they float on water occurs also in a Chinese version and in the Sanskrit *Divyāvadāna* [Winternitz 1933]. Computationally, DharmaNexus records extensive Pali text reuse with the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as low-scoring automated cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Dhāraṇīsaṃgraha* and a Tibetan canonical text [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): San Lo Mvu 44 The Jātaka of Amarā, the Smith’s Daughter; Ja 546 Vidhurajātaka
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§2.4–4.4 ↔ §2522–2526)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): Dhāraṇīsaṃgraha (SA_K12_n2949u) [sa]; BO_K01_D0001-4_H0001-4 [bo]

- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus computed parallels for ja387 — Reports Pali-internal text reuse with Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā and alignments with Dhāraṇīsaṃgraha and a Tibetan text.
- [Dutt 1956] Nalinaksha Dutt, Development of Buddhism in Uttar Pradesh (1956) — Cites the text for its mention of the head of the smith guild (kammārajetthaka).
- [Winternitz 1933] Maurice Winternitz, History of Indian Literature II (1933) — Notes Chinese and Divyāvadāna parallels featuring an artistic smith whose needles float on water.
- [Fausböll 1883] V. Fausböll, Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 3 (1883) — Supplies the conclusion and samodhāna identifying the smith's daughter as Rāhulamātā and the wise smith as the Bodhisatta.
